missiles.name: Agni-V
facts: Three-stage solid-fueled road-mobile ICBM developed by India's DRDO.
Equipped with advanced ring-laser gyros and MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicle) capability.
Reaches terminal speeds of approximately Mach 24 (nearly 29,400 km/h).

missiles.name: Agni-IV
facts: Two-stage solid-propellant ballistic missile bridging India's medium and intercontinental strike wings.
Features composite rocket motor casings for significantly lighter launch weight.
Re-entry heat shield withstands exterior friction temperatures above 4,000°C.

missiles.name: Agni-III
facts: Compact 17-meter two-stage solid-fuel missile designed for rapid deployment from rail launchers.
High payload capacity capable of carrying heavy nuclear warhead packages.
Forms the backbone of the Strategic Forces Command regional deterrence.

missiles.name: Agni-II
facts: Two-stage solid-propellant road and rail mobile ballistic missile.
Features post-boost vehicle control fins for high-accuracy terminal trajectory correction.
Tested extensively with high operational reliability under the SFC.

missiles.name: Agni-Prime (Agni-P)
facts: Next-generation canisterized solid-fuel missile that can be stored for years and launched on minutes' notice.
Features dual-redundant navigation and guidance systems with thrust-vector control.
Weighs 50% less than Agni-II despite having equivalent operational strike range.

missiles.name: BrahMos Block-III / ER
facts: Joint Indo-Russian development and the world's fastest operational ramjet supersonic cruise missile.
Flies sea-skimming trajectories as low as 3 to 10 meters before an aggressive terminal dive.
Extended Range (ER) variant upgrades range to 800 km with precision radar seeker guidance.

missiles.name: BrahMos-II (Hypersonic)
facts: Scramjet-powered hypersonic cruise missile engineered to cruise at Mach 7 to Mach 8.
Designed to penetrate dense anti-ballistic and air-defense radar umbrellas through pure velocity.
Kinetic energy upon impact amplifies damage significantly beyond chemical explosives.

missiles.name: Nirbhay
facts: All-weather stealth subsonic land-attack cruise missile developed by ADE/DRDO.
Equipped with ring-laser gyro INS, GPS/NAVIC satellite guidance, and RF seeker for terminal accuracy.
Loiters over target zone before executing precision strike.

missiles.name: Pralay Tactical Ballistic
facts: Canisterized quasi-ballistic surface-to-surface missile designed for conventional battlefield strikes.
Performs mid-course maneuvers using aerodynamic thrusters to defeat interceptor air-defense systems.
Carries penetration, blast-fragmentation, and submunition warheads up to 1,000 kg.

missiles.name: Shaurya Hypersonic
facts: Land-based derivative of India's Sagarika (K-15) submarine-launched ballistic missile.
Flies in the atmosphere at hypersonic speed, making radar detection and tracking exceedingly difficult.
Stored in composite canisters mounted on all-terrain road trucks.

missiles.name: K-4 SLBM
facts: Nuclear-capable submarine-launched ballistic missile deployed aboard INS Arihant-class SSBNs.
Equipped with advanced 3D thrust vectoring control for vertical underwater ejection.
Provides India with a survivable, guaranteed second-strike nuclear deterrence capability.

missiles.name: Prithvi-II
facts: First ballistic missile developed under India's Integrated Guided Missile Development Program (IGMDP).
Uses twin liquid-fuel rocket engines with advanced inertial strap-down guidance.
Capable of carrying conventional or nuclear warheads with CEP under 10 meters.

missiles.name: LGM-30G Minuteman III
facts: Forms the hardened silo-based land leg of the United States nuclear triad.
Capable of launching within 60 seconds of receiving authenticated presidential launch codes.
Carries the W78 (335 kt) or W87 (300 kt) thermonuclear warhead in a precision Mark 12A/21 RV.

missiles.name: UGM-133A Trident II D5 (US)
facts: Deploys aboard Ohio-class ballistic missile submarines with extraordinary navigational accuracy.
Each missile can deploy up to 8 MIRV thermonuclear warheads (W76-1 90kt or W88 455kt).
Over 180 consecutive successful test flights, representing the gold standard of SLBM reliability.

missiles.name: BGM-109 Tomahawk Block V
facts: Premier US long-range all-weather precision strike cruise missile launched from cruisers and submarines.
Uses GPS, TERCOM (Terrain Contour Matching), and optical DSMAC for sub-meter terminal accuracy.
Block V includes multi-mode seekers capable of striking moving maritime targets at sea.

missiles.name: AGM-158B JASSM-ER
facts: Low-observable radar-evading standoff missile carried by B-1B, B-52H, F-15E, F-16, and F-35.
Equipped with a dual-mode penetrator warhead designed to shatter hardened underground command bunkers.
Employs an imaging infrared (IIR) seeker that visually verifies the target prior to impact.

missiles.name: AGM-114 Hellfire
facts: Precision laser-guided anti-armor and counter-insurgency missile fired from Apache helicopters and MQ-9 Reapers.
Carries an 8 kg shaped-charge tandem warhead designed to defeat explosive reactive armor.
Originally stood for 'Heliborne Laser, Fire-and-Forget Missile'.

missiles.name: MGM-140 ATACMS
facts: Fired from M142 HIMARS and M270 MLRS tracked and wheeled mobile launchers.
Carries either a 227 kg unitary blast-frag warhead or APAM submunitions.
Flies a semi-ballistic trajectory using GPS and ring-laser gyros to avoid air defense systems.

missiles.name: Precision Strike Missile (PrSM)
facts: US Army successor to ATACMS fitting two missiles per HIMARS launcher pod instead of one.
Compliant with the repealed INF Treaty limit, hitting pinpoint targets out to 500 km.
Capable of attacking surface warships and air defense batteries in contested anti-access environments.

missiles.name: AGM-86B ALCM
facts: Primary nuclear standoff cruise missile of the US Air Force B-52H Stratofortress fleet.
Carries the W80-1 variable-yield thermonuclear warhead (5 to 150 kt).
Navigates via terrain-following radar at tree-top level to stay under Soviet and modern air radars.

missiles.name: RIM-161 Standard Missile 3 (SM-3)
facts: Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense weapon capable of intercepting short to intermediate-range ballistic missiles in space.
Uses a Kinetic Warhead (hit-to-kill vehicle) with over 130 megajoules of structural kinetic impact energy.
Has successfully intercepted and destroyed decaying satellites in low Earth orbit.

missiles.name: RGM-84 Harpoon Block II
facts: Standard anti-ship missile used by the US Navy and over 30 allied nations for four decades.
Employs active radar homing and low-altitude sea-skimming cruising profile.
Block II upgrades added GPS guidance enabling precision strikes on land-based coastal batteries.

missiles.name: RS-28 Sarmat (Satan II)
facts: World's largest liquid-fueled super-heavy ICBM weighing over 208 metric tons.
Capable of flying fractional orbital trajectories over the South Pole to bypass northern radar arcs.
Can carry up to 10 heavy MIRVs, 15 lighter MIRVs, or up to 3 Avangard hypersonic glide vehicles.

missiles.name: RS-24 Yars
facts: Core of the Russian Strategic Rocket Forces mobile deterrent, carried on 16-wheeled MZKT transports.
Armed with 3 to 4 independently targetable MIRVs and advanced penetration decoy systems.
Solid propellant design allows rapid cold-launch from hidden forest dispersal areas.

missiles.name: R-36M2 Voyevoda (SS-18 Satan)
facts: Legendary Soviet heavy ICBM designed to eliminate hardened NATO missile silos and command bunkers.
Can carry a massive single 20-megaton city-buster warhead or 10 heavy thermonuclear MIRVs.
Housed in super-hardened silos rated to withstand direct near-miss nuclear overpressures.

missiles.name: RSM-56 Bulava
facts: Primary armament of Russia's Borei-class fourth-generation nuclear ballistic missile submarines.
Features low-trajectory flight capability and defensive decoys to confuse space tracking sensors.
Carries 6 to 10 maneuverable nuclear warheads with autonomous celestial guidance.

missiles.name: 9M723 Iskander-M
facts: Road-mobile quasi-ballistic missile capable of pulling 30g evasive maneuvers in terminal descent.
Employs optical and radar correlator seekers providing circular error probable (CEP) under 5 meters.
Can be fitted with thermonuclear, bunker-buster, EMP, or cluster munitions.

missiles.name: Kh-47M2 Kinzhal
facts: Launched at high altitude from MiG-31K interceptors and Tu-22M3 strategic bombers.
Accelerates to Mach 10 while retaining full aerodynamic control surface maneuvering.
Used operationally in Ukraine against high-value underground ammunition depots and command centers.

missiles.name: 3M22 Zircon
facts: Fires from shipboard UKSK vertical launch systems and Yasen-M nuclear submarines.
Scramjet engine sustains Mach 8-9 flight within a plasma cloud that absorbs radar emissions.
Leaves modern shipboard close-in weapon systems (CIWS) virtually zero reaction window.

missiles.name: 3M-54 Kalibr
facts: Russia's counterpart to the US Tomahawk cruise missile, launched from frigates, corvettes, and subs.
Navigates around natural topographical contours to evade early warning radar networks.
Anti-ship variant features a supersonic Mach 2.9 rocket booster for the final 20 km sprint.

missiles.name: Kh-101 Stealth Cruise
facts: Strategic low-observable cruise missile with flattened radar-absorbent fuselage cross section.
Carried internally by Tu-160 Blackjack and externally by Tu-95MS Bear heavy bombers.
Employs Otblesk-U electro-optical scene matching system for final targeting accuracy.

missiles.name: DF-41 (Dongfeng-41)
facts: China's most powerful road and rail mobile solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile.
Operational strike range of 15,000 km covers the entire continental United States and Europe.
Can carry up to 10 MIRV nuclear warheads along with sophisticated chaff and decoy suites.

missiles.name: DF-31AG
facts: Upgraded variant of DF-31 mounted on an 8-axle off-road all-terrain transporter-erector-launcher (TEL).
Can launch from unpaved roads and remote wilderness, vastly increasing survivability.
Equipped with MIRV technology and terminal maneuver capability.

missiles.name: DF-26B (Guam Killer)
facts: Hot-swappable dual-capable missile system supporting both conventional precision and nuclear warheads.
Nicknamed the 'Guam Killer' due to its ability to strike major US military bases in the second island chain.
Equipped with active radar terminal seeker capable of striking moving aircraft carriers.

missiles.name: DF-21D (Carrier Killer)
facts: World's first operational anti-ship ballistic missile designed specifically to defeat aircraft carriers.
Terminal radar and optical seekers correlate the target position as the reentry vehicle dives at Mach 10.
Key pillar of China's Anti-Access/Area Denial (A2/AD) maritime strategy in the Western Pacific.

missiles.name: DF-17 Hypersonic Glide Vehicle
facts: Boosted into high atmosphere by a ballistic rocket before detaching the DF-ZF hypersonic waverider.
Glides at extreme speeds through the upper atmosphere, executing unpredictably shaped lateral turns.
Renders traditional parabolic ballistic missile defense radars and interceptors largely ineffective.

missiles.name: JL-3 (Julang-3)
facts: China's third-generation intercontinental SLBM deployed on Type 094 and Type 096 SSBNs.
Allows Chinese submarines to strike targets in the continental United States from protected bastions in the South China Sea.
Carries up to 6 MIRV nuclear warheads.

missiles.name: CJ-10 (Changjian-10)
facts: Long-range precision land-attack cruise missile developed by the Second Academy of CASIC.
Uses inertial guidance combined with BeiDou satellite navigation and scene matching.
Carries high-explosive unitary, thermobaric, or submunition warheads.

missiles.name: M51 SLBM
facts: Forms the primary sea-based component of France's independent nuclear deterrent (Force de frappe).
Deployed aboard Triomphant-class nuclear ballistic submarines with 16 missiles per boat.
Carries 6 to 10 TNO (Tête Nucléaire Océanique) thermonuclear warheads per missile.

missiles.name: ASMP-A
facts: Airborne leg of the French nuclear deterrent, carried exclusively by Dassault Rafale fighters.
Powered by an integral ramjet engine cruising at Mach 3 at high altitude or Mach 2 at sea level.
Designed to deliver an 'ultime avertissement' (final nuclear warning) strike.

missiles.name: Storm Shadow / SCALP-EG
facts: Joint UK-French long-range precision standoff weapon manufactured by MBDA.
Equipped with the BROACH two-stage bunker-penetrating warhead to defeat reinforced bridges and bunkers.
Used extensively by Ukraine with high interception resistance against Russian air defense systems.

missiles.name: Exocet MM40 Block 3
facts: One of the world's most famous combat-proven anti-ship missile systems.
Block 3 adds a turbojet engine extending range to 200 km and GPS waypoint coastal navigation.
Flies just 1 to 2 meters above wave crests during terminal attack to stay hidden from radar.

missiles.name: Trident II D5 (United Kingdom)
facts: Sole nuclear weapons system in the British armed forces, carried aboard Vanguard-class SSBNs.
Operated under Operation Relentless ensuring Continuous At-Sea Deterrence (CASD) since 1969.
Carries British-assembled thermonuclear warheads developed at AWE Aldermaston.

missiles.name: Sea Viper / Aster 30
facts: Primary anti-air and anti-missile defense weapon of the Royal Navy Type 45 Daring-class destroyers.
Features PIF-PAF lateral thrusters in the warhead section for 60g terminal intercept maneuvers.
Demonstrated successful combat intercepts against Houthi anti-ship ballistic missiles in the Red Sea.

missiles.name: Brimstone 2
facts: Dual-mode millimeter-wave radar and semi-active laser guided anti-armor missile.
Designed for salvo firing ('fire-and-forget') against moving armor formations with minimal collateral damage.
Deployed from Eurofighter Typhoon, fast attack boats, and ground-based mobile launchers.

missiles.name: Jericho III
facts: Three-stage solid-propellant ballistic missile forming the strategic backbone of Israel's nuclear deterrent.
Based in hardened underground caves and silos at Sdot Micha Airbase.
Capable of carrying a 1,000 kg thermonuclear warhead or 2-3 MIRVs across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia.

missiles.name: Popeye Turbo SLCM
facts: Turbojet-powered strategic standoff missile deployed aboard Israeli Dolphin-class AIP submarines.
Equipped with a sealed nuclear warhead for survivable second-strike deterrence in the Mediterranean.
Fired through specially expanded 650 mm submarine torpedo tubes.

missiles.name: Delilah Standoff
facts: Precision loitering missile designed to hunt mobile surface-to-air missile radar systems.
Features a man-in-the-loop electro-optical seeker allowing the operator to redirect or abort the attack.
Can loiter over the target area for extended duration before initiating a dive attack.

missiles.name: Khorramshahr-4 (Kheibar)
facts: Iran's most advanced liquid-fueled ballistic missile powered by hypergolic storable propellants.
Reaches Mach 16 outside the atmosphere and Mach 8 inside the atmosphere during final dive.
Carries a massive 1,500 kg warhead with mid-course steering engines that eliminate radar detection fins.

missiles.name: Fattah-1 Hypersonic
facts: Unveiled by the IRGC Aerospace Force as Iran's first hypersonic missile with a movable nozzle reentry vehicle.
Claims terminal maneuvering velocity of Mach 13 to defeat Arrow-3 and Patriot interceptor systems.
Uses solid-propellant spherical rocket motor inside the warhead for high-altitude evasive bursts.

missiles.name: Sejjil-2
facts: Two-stage solid-propellant MRBM offering vastly superior launch readiness compared to liquid-fueled Shahab systems.
Requires minutes to prepare for launch from mobile TELs, minimizing pre-launch vulnerability.
High terminal velocity and steep reentry angle challenge regional missile defense systems.

missiles.name: Hwasong-17 (Monster ICBM)
facts: World's largest road-mobile liquid-fueled ICBM, carried on an 11-axle heavy transport vehicle.
Tested on lofted trajectories exceeding 6,000 km altitude, demonstrating full strike coverage of the United States.
Believed to be designed for carrying multiple nuclear warheads (MIRVs) and penetration aids.

missiles.name: Hwasong-15
facts: Two-stage liquid-propellant ICBM first launched successfully in November 2017.
Powered by twin gimballed combustion chamber rocket engines with vernier thrusters.
Capable of delivering a super-large heavy thermonuclear warhead to any location in North America.

missiles.name: KN-23 (Hwasong-11Ga)
facts: Solid-fueled quasi-ballistic missile strongly resembling the Russian Iskander-M and South Korean Hyunmoo-2B.
Flies a depressed aero-ballistic trajectory with terminal pull-up maneuvers to escape radar tracking.
Exported and fired in active combat operations during European theater warfare.

missiles.name: Taepodong-2 / Unha-3
facts: Three-stage liquid-fueled rocket based on clustered Nodong engine technology.
Demonstrated satellite orbital insertion capability in 2012 and 2016.
Serves as the structural design basis for early North Korean strategic ICBM development.

missiles.name: Hyunmoo-V (Monster Missile)
facts: World's heaviest conventional ballistic warhead carrying up to 8 to 9 metric tons of high explosive.
Engineered to generate earth-penetrating kinetic shockwaves collapsing bunkers 100 meters underground.
Nicknamed the 'Monster Missile' of the Republic of Korea Armed Forces.

missiles.name: Taurus KEPD 350
facts: Joint German-Swedish precision standoff cruise missile developed by Taurus Systems.
Equipped with MEPHISTO multi-stage penetrator warhead that counts void layers before detonation.
Operated by Germany, Spain, and South Korea for hardened bridge and command center neutralisation.

missiles.name: Sagarika (K-15) SLBM
facts: Underwater-launched ballistic missile providing India's sea-based nuclear deterrence aboard INS Arihant.
Underwater gas booster launches the missile to the ocean surface before the rocket motor ignites.
Compact two-stage solid-fuel motor designed and manufactured by DRDO.
